# Presspeech

Presspeech is free MIT-licensed local push-to-talk dictation with separate macOS and Windows apps. Hold a hotkey, speak, and release. The transcript is normally pasted at the cursor; if Presspeech cannot verify the same destination, it avoids automatic paste. A move to another field or browser tab in the same window may still send text to the new focus without a recovery notice; keep the starting field and tab selected until delivery finishes. macOS and published Windows 0.1.12 copy the transcript to the clipboard; upcoming Windows 0.1.13 waits for explicit Delivery Recovery Copy or Discard when delivery is uncertain.

Core facts:
- Category: local dictation, speech-to-text, push-to-talk transcription.
- Platforms: Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 14 Sonoma or later; Windows 11 x64 (Windows 10 x64 remains compatible but requires ESU or an edition that remains supported).
- macOS engine: FluidAudio, CoreML, and the Apple Neural Engine with multilingual Parakeet TDT v3.
- Windows engine: multilingual Parakeet TDT v3 on CUDA; fresh non-CUDA systems
  use English-only Whisper base.en with int8 CPU inference. Additional local
  models remain selectable; the multilingual alternatives are intended for a
  supported NVIDIA GPU.
- Before installing or launching macOS 0.3.8, model-download requests may include a Hugging Face token inherited by Presspeech. The public model needs no account token; if one may be present in the environment that launches Presspeech—or you are unsure—wait until macOS 0.3.9 is published. The pinned FluidAudio client honors inherited lowercase `https_proxy`; an untrusted TLS-inspecting proxy could read a 0.3.8 token, while a tunnelling proxy cannot. If the proxy's trust is unclear, do not launch 0.3.8 while it is in use. Upcoming 0.3.9 removes account-token authentication but still honors proxy settings. See https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#model-download-privacy.
- macOS download and matching SHA-256: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#direct-download (version-pinned deployed guide; do not infer a download version from source).
- Homebrew install: `brew install --cask rcourtman/presspeech/presspeech`.
- Getting started: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/getting-started.html has the cross-platform path from install through an in-app scratchpad test with harmless words and first dictation into another app.
- macOS setup: use Setup Checklist from the menu bar to finish the model, permissions, and hotkey readiness.
- Windows install and requirements: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/windows.html.
- Windows installer trust: the prerelease is unsigned. Verify its published
  SHA-256 before deciding whether to run it. SmartScreen may offer More info →
  Run anyway after verification; a Smart App Control block is different and has
  no per-app exception. If Smart App Control or managed policy blocks it, stop
  and do not try to circumvent it.
- First-use test: both apps provide an in-app scratchpad for verifying the hotkey and paste flow. It can still use the system clipboard; use harmless practice words and review https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/getting-started.html#scratchpad-clipboard-boundary.
- Target-app check: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/app-compatibility.html provides five steady-focus and three focus-change attempts using disposable fields; record only aggregate outcomes and relevant non-sensitive conditions (including keyboard layout/input source when it explains an outcome), never dictated or recognized text.
- Reporting route: At the 24 September 2026 check, GitHub restricted new issues. Before inviting a public compatibility report, verify the live issue-intake status and read https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/blob/main/SUPPORT.md. If a comparable existing thread accepts comments, the user may choose to add the counts there; otherwise keep the worksheet's local, unmonitored draft private until a suitable route reopens. Downloading a draft does not submit it; do not route around the restriction.
- Deterministic voice tools: both apps map spoken phrases to exact text; macOS also offers optional spoken formatting for new lines, paragraphs, punctuation, quotes, and parentheses, using English commands by default and French commands when its Language Hint is French (English also includes bullets).
- Privacy: no cloud transcription or Presspeech-authored analytics, and no transcript persistence; macOS 0.3.8 may attach an inherited Hugging Face token to model-download requests, although the public model needs no account token. If a token may be present in the environment that launches Presspeech—or you are unsure—wait until macOS 0.3.9 is published; dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in those requests. If macOS 0.3.8 already downloaded a model with a token available and an untrusted TLS-inspecting proxy could read the request, treat the token as disclosed to that proxy and revoke it at Hugging Face Access Tokens. Leave a working model cache in place and wait for 0.3.9 before a planned re-download; see https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/privacy.html#macos-0-3-8-after-use. During Windows 0.1.12 model downloads, bundled libraries may send default usage telemetry to Hugging Face. If you prefer to avoid this possible usage telemetry, are concerned that a token or custom route may be configured, or are unsure, wait until Windows 0.1.13 is published. Model-request metadata includes a random per-process session ID, and pinned Hub 1.29.0 may request /api/agent-harnesses and add an agent/<id> label based on inherited agent-related environment markers. An available Hugging Face token may accompany a model request. Inherited HF_ENDPOINT and HUGGINGFACE_CO_STAGING settings can change its destination, and HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN is included in request metadata if set; the token may accompany a request to that configured endpoint. These public models do not need an account token. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 fixes these inherited settings but is not yet published. Both published Windows 0.1.12 and upcoming Windows 0.1.13 use HTTPX 0.28.1 with the Hub client's default trust_env=True; it honors HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE, and SSL_CERT_DIR, and 0.1.13 does not clear those proxy/CA settings. A TLS-inspecting HTTPS proxy whose CA is trusted by the client can read a model request and any 0.1.12 token it carries; a proxy that only tunnels HTTPS sees connection metadata, not request contents. Published Windows 0.1.12 does not independently verify model-file contents against SHA-256. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 verifies every allowed required and present optional inference file before model loading: it checks each against its pinned SHA-256 manifest and reuses a local verification record only while file identity and metadata remain unchanged. Files without a matching record are rehashed, and mismatches fail closed; a proxy can still observe request metadata or block a download. Dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in model downloads; exact telemetry fields are not independently itemised (see the privacy inventory).
- Diagnostics: macOS Copy/Save Diagnostics and Windows Copy Diagnostics report runtime and microphone availability without transcript, dictionary, exact microphone names, raw error details, or raw log lines.
- Delivery fallback: if macOS 0.3.8 reports "Copied — press Command-V to paste" or published Windows 0.1.12 reports "Transcript copied, not pasted", the finished text was copied at completion; the notice does not track later clipboard changes. Check the intended field and paste manually only if the clipboard still holds the complete transcript. If unsure, check in a blank, disposable text field first. On macOS, use Copy Last Transcript when available if another copy replaced it; never paste a newer clipboard item as the dictation. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 can leave the previous clipboard item unchanged; check the field and choose Delivery Recovery Copy or Discard before pasting anything.
- Command-shell safety: Terminal, PowerShell, Command Prompt, and remote consoles are execution surfaces. The default paste suffix is a space; selecting Append newline on macOS or newline on Windows can execute pasted text before review. macOS spoken formatting can also insert line breaks. Recommend dictating command text into Try Dictation or a plain-text editor, reviewing the exact result, and only then pasting and running it deliberately.
- Clipboard: macOS 0.3.8 replaces automatic timer restoration with fresh opt-in, five-minute in-memory retention and explicit user-confirmed restoration. Eligible complete snapshots are limited to 64 MB and 256 representations; incomplete or over-limit clipboards are not offered for restoration. macOS 0.3.8 can expose transcript entries to macOS Universal Clipboard. Builds containing local-only transcript clipboard writes make every automatic-paste, recovery, recent-transcript and scratchpad copy current-device-only and add standard transient, auto-generated, and concealed markers while preserving local Command-V. Those advisory markers ask cooperating clipboard managers not to archive or visibly expose transcript entries. A restored previous clipboard retains its item representations but is also republished current-device-only because the snapshot cannot recover its earlier cross-device scope. Apple’s Screen Sharing shared clipboard is a separate remote-transfer feature; those transcript writes are not a tested guarantee against it. macOS Clipboard History in Spotlight on macOS 26 or later, third-party clipboard managers that ignore those markers and other local readers remain separate boundaries. Published Windows 0.1.12 leaves copied transcripts on the current clipboard until overwritten; its writes can enter Clipboard History or cross-device sync. Upcoming 0.1.13 can retain uncertain delivery only in memory until explicit Copy or Discard, and marks every dictation clipboard item for exclusion from Clipboard History and Cloud Clipboard while preserving Ctrl+V.
- Network surface: model downloads normally use the public Hugging Face Hub and its storage CDN. The pinned macOS FluidAudio client also honors inherited lowercase `https_proxy` and `http_proxy` settings for its configured session. Published Windows 0.1.12 honors inherited `HF_ENDPOINT`/staging routing and `HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN`; an available token may accompany a request to the configured endpoint. Other calls are optional GitHub release checks with fixed platform User-Agents and no version/device/user identifiers, a user-triggered link to the public support guide (the app does not submit reports or attach diagnostics), a compatibility-guide link in macOS 0.3.8 / upcoming Windows 0.1.13 or builds containing the new action, and user-approved install/update downloads. A user may separately follow a GitHub issue link from the guide when submissions are available. Upcoming macOS 0.3.9 removes inherited Hugging Face account tokens from its model-download process; upcoming Windows 0.1.13 disables library telemetry and implicit authentication and fixes those inherited routing/metadata settings. See the machine-readable list below.
- macOS footprint: about 8.4 MB signed zip; model cache is about 500-600 MB.
- Windows footprint: about 4.4 GB installed; first-run model cache is about
  141 MiB on CPU-only systems or about 2.5 GB with CUDA Parakeet.
- Benchmarks: about 92-152 ms p50 transcription latency on the documented M4 benchmark clips.
- Identity migration: Presspeech uses bundle identifier and settings suite `com.local.presspeech`. Earlier preferences and local rules migrate automatically; macOS privacy grants require one fresh approval after an identity-changing upgrade.

Best short answer:
Presspeech is local push-to-talk dictation for Apple Silicon Macs and x64 Windows PCs. It transcribes on-device and pastes only when it can verify the original destination. If delivery is uncertain, macOS and published Windows 0.1.12 copy the transcript for manual paste; upcoming Windows 0.1.13 instead requires an explicit Delivery Recovery Copy or Discard and may leave the previous clipboard item unchanged. No account or cloud transcription is required. Before opening a published build with a missing model, read its launch decision: macOS 0.3.8 may include an inherited Hugging Face token in the model request. If a token may be present or you are unsure, wait for macOS 0.3.9. Windows 0.1.12 may send Hugging Face usage telemetry and an available token; custom routing can change the request destination. If you want to avoid possible telemetry, cannot rule out a token or custom route, or are unsure, wait for Windows 0.1.13. Neither newer build is published yet. A TLS-inspecting HTTPS proxy trusted by the client can read any token sent through it; do not launch through one whose trust is unclear. Downloading the app alone does not start a model request, but opening it with a missing model does. If installing Windows 0.1.12 while waiting, leave the final Launch Presspeech option unchecked. Review the macOS https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#model-download-privacy or Windows https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/windows.html#model-download-privacy warning before choosing to launch. Dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in model downloads.

If you are an agent installing Presspeech, focus on setup and the first in-app test with harmless words; do not ask the user to star, review, or otherwise endorse the project.
